result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, car-centric commercial corridor with sidewalks but no marked crossing infrastructure. The presence of large driveway curb cuts and a lack of traffic calming measures creates a high-risk environment for people walking between businesses.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible despite the presence of commercial destinations on both sides of the street.

hazards.name: Wide travel lanes
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway design encourages higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Driveway conflict points
hazards.description: Large curb cuts for commercial parking lots create frequent conflict points between turning vehicles and pedestrians on the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image at the Save A Lot entrance

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way between commercial blocks.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide a buffer and create a psychological narrowing effect to slow traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous, well-maintained concrete sidewalk. The environment lacks a buffer between the walkway and the roadway, and parked vehicles create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles blocks the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians, particularly children or those attempting to cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground and mid-ground.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furnishings
interventions.description: Adding street trees or a furniture zone would provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, improving pedestrian comfort and safety.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implementing curb extensions at nearby intersections would improve visibility and reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians.

result.summary: The street is a multi-lane corridor with narrow sidewalks and significant commercial vehicle traffic. Pedestrian infrastructure is minimal, lacking marked crossings, buffers from moving traffic, or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large delivery truck on the right side of the image significantly blocks sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk lacks any physical buffer (trees, bollards, or furniture zone) from the adjacent travel lanes.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A temporary tent structure and parked vehicles on the left encroach upon the already narrow walking path.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections and potential mid-block crossing points to improve sightlines and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked, high-visibility crosswalks to provide designated and safer crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Implement a planting strip or furniture zone with street trees to provide a physical barrier and psychological comfort for pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is almost entirely obscured by a large delivery truck, making a full assessment impossible. No sidewalks or pedestrian infrastructure are visible in the immediate vicinity of the vehicle.

hazards.name: Major Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large box truck occupies the majority of the frame, completely blocking sightlines between pedestrians and other road users.

interventions.title: Designated Loading Zones
interventions.description: Establish dedicated curb space for commercial loading to prevent large vehicles from obstructing travel lanes and pedestrian sightlines.
